relevance_note: Case report of one boy with a GFAP variant and Alexander disease: "A de novo heterozygous mutation, NM_001242376.1:c.262 C > T;R88C in exon 1 of the GFAP".
method_note: Single-patient case report; output built by a short Python script whose spans were located in the paper by matching and then checked verbatim; every value was read by hand. In scope: the patient (label 'patient'; the paper calls him 'the proband', a role word); his father and uncle (HC above 2 SD, no clinical symptoms; father also tested negative); the other parent, tested negative ('neither of the parents carry the mutation'), labelled 'parent of patient' because the paper never names the mother; two previously published juvenile AxD patients with R88C attributed to 'Gorospe et al.' (the sentence cites [8, 14, 16, 17], a multi-paper citation that is not person-specific, and no Gorospe paper is in the reference list); and a previously published 3-month-old girl treated with steroids (ref [20]). The 22 Chinese children of ref [8] are group-level only and get no rows. No variant rows for the tested-negative parents. Gene for the Gorospe patients is taken from the paragraph's statement about GFAP mutations, as their sentence names no gene. Age at onset is the first reported symptom (seizures at 40 days), although the authors classify the disease as late-onset / type II with the vomiting presentation at 6 years; no age at diagnosis is stated. Checklist: 'spasticity or pyramidal signs' observed from exaggerated knee reflexes (3+) although the paper says the patient did not show spasticity; 'ataxia or cerebellar signs' left not reported (only ataxia is excluded); 'palatal tremor' excluded from 'Palatal myoclonus was not detected'; 'cognitive decline' excluded from 'A normal cognitive 9-year-old boy'; nasal tone speech not mapped to dysarthria or dysphonia; dysphagia not reported (only speech therapy 'to improve swallowing ability' and a weak gag reflex); garland changes not recorded as a periventricular rim; normal gaze does not exclude the composite eye-movement/diplopia item. Normal whole examinations (other cranial nerves, gastroenterological assessments, basic biochemical and metabolic tests) were recorded in the paper's own terms as excluded. Time-dependent EEG findings (abnormal in infancy, normal at about 6.5 years, scattered discharges at 8 years) are recorded as separate rows, not as a contradiction. Minor inconsistency: autonomic episodes are dated 'At the age of 6.5 years' in the case presentation and 'at the age of 6 years' in the Discussion; both rows kept.
